content.text:
We have 6 demos. Maybe enough. But let's consider if the held-out inputs might include edge cases like marker with no empty cells around, markers in same region (though rule says no overlap because walls separate; but verifier would process multiple seeds in same region and last would overwrite earlier because each BFS from seed fills its region, and later seeds overwrite earlier colors! Wait—the verifier code loops over seeds in order and does BFS from each through 0 cells. If two seeds are in the same connected empty region, both BFS would fill the same region, and the later seed's color would overwrite the earlier. The natural language rule says "If two markers' flood regions would never overlap (because X walls separate them)", implying in this task markers are always separated. But the verifier actually would handle overlapping by last-wins. However held-out inputs probably satisfy separation.

Our demos are all separated. Good.

But maybe we should demonstrate a case where a marker has no reachable empty cells? Not necessary.

We should finish teaching now. Six demos covering: single marker filling all; wall-bounded; two markers; multiple regions including unfilled region; separated quadrants. Good.
